newsitem.title: UK: Shareholders push for Greycoat asset sale.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders push for Greycoat asset sale.

text.p: Shareholders in British property company Greycoat will on Monday requisition an EGM to demand the sale of its 500 million stg portfolio.

A statement on Sunday night from UK Active Value Fund, IMP UKAV Inc and Chaddesley Investments Limited confirmed they would demand an EGM at which they would call upon the directors of Greycoat to seek the disposal of all the company's assets with a view to distributing the proceeds to shareholders.
The statement confirmed a report in the Sunday Times. The investment funds control an 11 percent stake in the company and are advised by Active Value Advisors LTD (AVA).

AVA said a controlled programme of disposals would enhance shareholder value significantly. A rising property market provides an excellent opportunity for disposals at or above current asset values over the next 18 months, AVA added.

"The time has come to unlock the value of Greycoat. The shares stand at a 23 percent discount to forecast 1997 NAV, despite the fact that Greycoat has a high quality portfolio," said Bryan Myerson of AVA.
"Having spoken to a number of shareholders, we believe that there is considerable support for our proposal which will enhance shareholder value," he added.
A spokesman for the funds said the EGM should take place in six weeks or so. No comment was available from Greycoat.
The move could herald the biggest auction of property in central London for many years.
